author: Tertullian

passages.original: satis ista de terrae nomine, in quo materiam intellegi uoluit. quod nomen unius elementi omnes sciunt, natura primum, dehinc scriptura docente, nisi si et Sileno illi apud Midam regem adseueranti de alio orbe credendum est, auctore Theopompo. sed et deos multos idem refert.
passages.english: Enough of this about the name "earth", under which he wanted matter to be understood. Everyone knows that this is the name of a single element, as nature teaches first and scripture afterwards, unless we are also to believe that Silenus who, before King Midas, asserted the existence of another world, on the authority of Theopompus. But the same [writer] also reports many gods.
passages.notes: The reference is to Theopompus' story (in the Philippica) of Silenus telling Midas about a continent beyond the known world. "idem refert" could refer to Silenus or to Theopompus; I have taken it as Theopompus, the nearer authority. "unius elementi" may mean "of one [particular] element", i.e. earth as one of the elements, rather than "a single element".
